title: tenant_default shadow table (from unqualified CREATE TABLE tenant in 031_adp04b_tenant_realm_binding.sql) causes schema drift; OutOfOrderMigration false-positive on cold-start db_test
affected_areas: any unqualified INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT against `tenant` issued while search_path includes a tenant schema before public
notes:
Discovered while implementing ISS-0100 (GitHub #357) Iteration 1 (GBL-086/102 guard scoping + helpers.zig SVC fixture hygiene). Two distinct, compounding pre-existing defects, both reproducible on main with zero ISS-0100 changes present (confirmed via baseline stash-and-compare):

(1) Shadow tenant_default.tenant table: migration 031_adp04b_tenant_realm_binding.sql contains an UNQUALIFIED `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tenant (...)`. Because this file is not GBL-prefixed, src/db/migrations.zig's per-schema skip logic (lines 196-207, GBL-prefix-only) does not exclude it from non-public schemas, so it creates a duplicate `tenant` table inside tenant_default (and presumably any other provisioned tenant schema). Later GBL-prefixed migrations that add columns to public.tenant (e.g. GBL-080's tenant_type) are, by design, never applied to this shadow copy. tests/integration/helpers.zig::configureTestSearchPath sets `search_path TO tenant_default,public` on every TestHarness.init(), so any unqualified `INSERT INTO tenant (...)` issued afterward (e.g. the SVC-01..04 fixture block in ensureDefaultOidcSeeds, prior to the ISS-0100 fix) silently resolves against the stale shadow table and fails once a GBL-only column is referenced (`column "tenant_type" of relation "tenant" does not exist`). Verified reproducible on both a long-lived warmed-up db_test and a freshly recreated one. Fixed locally within ISS-0100's own two files by schema-qualifying every `tenant` reference in ensureDefaultOidcSeeds as `public.tenant` -- but every OTHER unqualified reference to `tenant` anywhere in the codebase (other test helpers, migrations, application code) remains equally exposed.

(2) OutOfOrderMigration false positive on true cold-start: recreating db_test from a completely empty Docker volume and immediately running the full integration suite (zig build test-integration-svc, which aggregates all ~543 integration tests via tests/integration/main_test.zig) reproducibly fails the very first TestHarness.init() call with error.OutOfOrderMigration from src/db/migrations.zig. Confirmed via baseline (no ISS-0100 changes) comparison: identical failure on main. Does NOT reproduce when db_test is first fully migrated via the standalone `migrate` binary (BPM_DB_URL repointed at the test port) -- all 95 migrations apply cleanly for both public and tenant_default schemas that way -- then the test suite is run against that already-migrated state. Root cause not fully isolated; duplicate numeric migration-file prefixes exist on disk (050_tenant_hostnames.sql / 050_xc01_trace_id_audit.sql, and 056_onboarding_registry.sql / 056_xc03_configuration_repository_fix.sql) and are a candidate contributing factor, though not proven as the direct trigger under the strict-less-than out-of-order guard.

Neither defect blocks normal pipeline operation because db_test is a long-lived container that already has all migrations applied in practice; both are latent risks for any future environment reset, CI cold-start, or new-developer onboarding. Full evidence trail: baseline run (before ISS-0100 changes, warm db_test) = 462 pass / 7 skip / 74 fail (543 total); with only the mechanical helpers.zig SVC tenant_type addition and no schema-qualification fix = 132 pass / 404 fail (regression, cascading from (1)); with the schema-qualification fix added = 474 pass / 7 skip / 62 fail (543 total) -- an improvement over baseline, with all 62 remaining failures independently confirmed unrelated to tenant/tenant_type (they involve other tables: service_catalog.scope, onboarding_registry.realm_id, and various tnt_schema_isolation/ext02/obs05/adp0x tests -- pre-existing cold-start schema-drift/isolation issues, out of ISS-0100's scope).
candidate_resolution: For (1): either (a) add a migration that DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tenant_default.tenant (and any other already-provisioned tenant schema's copy) now that `tenant` is understood to be public-only/global, or (b) schema-qualify 031_adp04b_tenant_realm_binding.sql's CREATE TABLE as public.tenant so it can never create a per-schema copy again, or (c) extend src/db/migrations.zig's per-schema skip rule beyond GBL-prefix-only to cover any migration file operating on tables now understood to be global (tenant, tenant_schemas, onboarding_registry, etc.). For (2): needs further isolation -- start by resolving the duplicate 050/056 migration-number collisions (rename one file in each pair to the next free number) and re-test cold-start; if the false positive persists, instrument src/db/migrations.zig's out-of-order check to log the exact filename pair that triggers it on a cold run.
